conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes 'yes', stating that evidence supports that widespread community mask use can reduce SARS-CoV-2 infections, and specifically notes that 'no' is not supported as a general conclusion.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: yes—evidence supports that widespread community mask use can reduce SARS‑CoV‑2 infections, though the average effect is modest and depends on mask type, fit, and consistent use.** “No” is not supported as a general conclusion.

The strongest direct evidence is a cluster-randomized trial in 600 rural Bangladeshi villages (342,126 adults). A community promotion program increased observed mask use and reduced *symptomatic, serologically confirmed* infections by about 9%; benefits were clearer for surgical than cloth masks and among older adults. Because it randomized whole communities, this directly addresses population-level use—not merely whether a mask protects its wearer.  
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9036942/

Population-level observational modeling across regions on six continents likewise estimated that average mask wearing corresponded to a 19% lower transmission rate (R). This supports a population benefit, but cannot fully separate masking from other behavior and policy changes, so it is less decisive than randomization.  
https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2119266119

The uncertainty behind skeptical claims is real: a Cochrane review found randomized evidence on masks for respiratory viruses did not show a clear reduction overall, with low adherence, heterogeneous interventions, and limited COVID-specific evidence. That finding means the evidence was insufficient to precisely quantify the effect in those trials; it does **not** demonstrate that masks cannot work, particularly when many people wear them properly.  
https://www.cochranelibrary.com/cdsr/doi/10.1002/14651858.CD006207.pub6/full

A 2023 systematic review similarly assesses evidence across individual masking, mask types, and mandates, underscoring that study designs and real-world compliance limit certainty about the exact effect size.  

https://royalsocietypublishing.org/rsta/article/381/2257/20230133/112518/Effectiveness-of-face-masks-for-reducing
